candidates.tagline: America's highway — not built for America's July
candidates.story: On July 4th, 2026, record heat caused a concrete section of I-97 near Baltimore to buckle and thrust broken slabs and exposed rebar upward across all three northbound lanes; engineers note the road was designed to historical temperature specs that assumed modern July heat would never occur.
candidates.why_funny: American infrastructure failed spectacularly on Independence Day because mid-20th century engineers built roads for a climate that no longer exists — and the fix takes six to nine hours on a holiday weekend.
candidates.alt: Buckled concrete slabs with rebar pushed upward across northbound lanes of Interstate 97 in Anne Arundel County, Maryland, after extreme July 4th heat caused the pavement to blow out

candidates.tagline: Projected 77 million subscribers. Got 30 million. Fired 3,200.
candidates.story: Microsoft publicly projected Xbox Game Pass would reach 77 million subscribers by 2026 — a target disclosed to regulators during their $70 billion Activision acquisition — but the service currently has just 30 million after a botched 50% price hike drove a mass exodus; on July 6, 2026, Xbox fired 3,200 employees and shut five studios.
candidates.why_funny: They used 'we'll have 77 million subscribers' to justify buying the world's biggest game publisher, missed by 61%, then filed 3,200 employees out the door — turning the most over-confident pitch to antitrust regulators in gaming history into pink slips.
candidates.alt: Original first-generation Xbox Duke controller photographed against a white background, showing the large oval form factor and green Xbox logo button
